svg.title: Model-based importance of initial phase state, processing and exposure for hydroxyapatite evolution in simulated body fluid
svg.desc: Panel a: flow diagram of relative feature importance. Initial phases 65.5%, structural order 13.9%, processing and exposure 20.6%. Panel b: hydroxyapatite fraction before and after 21 days in SBF for five sintering temperatures. Panel c: net change in hydroxyapatite fraction.
svg.text: From initial state to bioactive response: what matters most
Apatite–wollastonite (AW) glass-ceramics · immersion in simulated body fluid (SBF) · importances normalised to 100%
Ribbon height is proportional to relative importance; the three groups sum to 100%
Note: sintering temperature acts twice. Directly (17.9%) and by setting the initial phase assemblage (see panel b).
HA fraction before and after SBF
The initial HA fraction is non-monotonic in T: 37.3 → 6.7 → 22.4 → 20.2 → 12.4 wt%
Net change in HA after 21 days in SBF
Δ = day 21 − day 0: gain at 700, 800 and 1000 °C; loss at 900 and 1100 °C
Initial phases carry 65.5% of the model importance
It acts directly (17.9%) and by setting the initial
HA fraction, which falls from 37.3 to 6.7 wt%
between 700 and 800 °C and then varies non-
SBF soaking time carries only 2.7%. Confirm that
time was actually varied before reading this as
Figure 1 | Model-based importance of initial state, processing and exposure for hydroxyapatite (HA) evolution of apatite–wollastonite (AW) glass-
ceramics in simulated body fluid (SBF). (a) Flow diagram of relative feature importance (normalised to 100%); ribbon height is proportional to
importance and features are grouped into initial phases, structural order and processing/exposure. (b) HA fraction before (day 0) and after (day 21)
SBF immersion at five sintering temperatures. (c) Net change in HA fraction, Δ = day 21 − day 0 (green, gain; orange, loss). The analysis is
descriptive (n = 5 sintering temperatures); importances are model-dependent and are not causal estimates.
